summary: This is a well-scoped, additive Phase 6 deliverable: a compliance-tracker-only workflow status-transition validator (audit_pipeline_workflow_transitions.py + a hand-authored TRANSITION_RULES_2026-07-24.yaml) and an ai-governance promptfoo slice (extract_production_prompts_ai_governance.py + 5 promptfoo suites + audit_pipeline_ai_governance.py) that tests real, drizzle-migration-extracted production system prompts with fully deterministic assertions (schema/javascript, zero llm-rubric). I independently re-ran both pipelines against the live compliance-tracker checkout on disk rather than trusting the self-report: the workflow validator reproduced exactly the claimed 9/9 findings (severities {low:8, medium:1}), and spot-checking verifyPunchListItemClosed/reviewSubmittal against the actual source confirmed the rule file's claims (comment claims a review sequence that the code never actually guards) are accurate, not fabricated. The ai-governance pipeline reproduced exactly the claimed 8 findings across the 5 suites using the committed .last_result.json artifacts, and I verified the injection-resistance finding (score=999 bypassing the prompt's declared 0-100 bound) is real in the cached transcript, that stripJsonFence() in the shared assertions helper is a verbatim copy of the real production function in llm-client.ts, and that the extracted prompt .txt files match what the extraction script deterministically re-derives from the real drizzle SQL. No secrets appear in the cached .last_result.json files (HTTP headers are redacted), all DB writes are parameterized (no SQL injection), subprocess calls use argument lists (no shell injection) against a hardcoded suite list, and the diff touches no migrations/schema/auth/permission/security/.env paths and no .github/workflows/** files, consistent with the tier1 pre-classification. Architecture (shared audit_findings/audit_runs SQLite tables, fcntl write-lock, upsert-by-finding_id) matches the pattern already established by prior phases. This is genuine, verifiable work, not a claim-only stub.
